FILING_DESTINATION.detail: The registry's destination is {kind: clerk, name: 'Circuit clerk of the county of arrest or charge', detail: 'File with the circuit clerk in each county where an arrest occurred or a charge was brought. The clerk performs service under section 5.2(d)(4).'}. The guide carries it under 'Where this is filed', naming what to file together (Request, Case List, any Additional Cases forms and the proposed Order), the county-by-county rule, and the AOIC flattening requirement for e-filing, and repeats the county rule and the Cook County district rule in the service section.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Both are stated in the record's own words under 'What it costs, and the waiver': a circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected, ISP charging nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order, county totals commonly roughly $60 to $235 with McLean County publishing $136, and the instruction to treat every figure as county-specific. The waiver is shipped, not merely named: the Supreme Court Rule 298 Application for Waiver of Court Fees is component 4, rendered as packet pages 10-13, and the guide states that section 5.2(d)(1) requires no fee where a Rule 298 order has been obtained or the fee is otherwise waived. The guide also states that the packet makes none of the waiver form's financial statements and lists all 46 of its check boxes as the participant's, which is the defect VF05 raised and FIX118 repaired in its second round.

SERVICE.detail: '## Who serves, and how' names the method - 'The circuit court clerk serves, under section 5.2(d)(4). The participant serves no one.' - and the recipients - the State's Attorney, the Illinois State Police, the arresting agency, and for municipal ordinance violations the chief legal officer - with the 60-day objection period under section 5.2(d)(5)(B) and the rule that absent an objection the court shall enter an order granting or denying under section 5.2(d)(6)(B). It adds that a separate flattened packet is filed with the clerk in each county, that Cook County filings go to the district matching the case, that a hearing date is added only when the clerk or court supplies it, and that court-owned service and order fields are not to be completed. I confirmed from the bytes that no service or certificate-of-service field is written.

ROUTE_IDENTITY.detail: The route key obligation:track-pathway:LA:la-985-expungement-by-redaction:expungement-by-redaction-for-multi-person-records is identical in the MASTER_QUEUE.json family row, production-field-map.json and packet-set-manifest.json. The relief is stated on the face of the delivered paper, which is what this route needs, because Article 985 relief has no election box: packet page 1 is titled 'ARTICLE 989 MOTION FOR EXPUNGEMENT, REQUESTING EXPUNGEMENT BY REDACTION UNDER ARTICLE 985' and prays for it, page 5 is titled 'ARTICLE 992 ORDER OF EXPUNGEMENT, CARRYING THE ARTICLE 985 REDACTION PARAGRAPH', and page 6 carries the dedicated Article 985 redaction section. That is exactly what the memo's legalDesignDecision limitation instructs: 'Use the Art. 989 motion and select the redaction option in the Art. 992 order, which contains a dedicated redaction paragraph. Do not create a custom redaction pleading.' The motion itself prints the reason on page 1 - Article 986 provides that only the statutory forms shall be used, so there is no separate redaction motion.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.detail: What binds, binds. The receipt declares two source binaries and both recompute exactly against the 501-file Master Library index by content: 0e455d3decea4b9e6299e1d39ceeb2b19ddaad93de19b2faa38d311f2d989ea2 = STATES/LA/05_SOURCE_GATED/...LA-CCRP-ART-993 article-993-supplemental-sheet..., and 13396bb180962be61788f0f7dd965fe4095d2262506b097623a86a6268e7a65a = ...LA-CCRP-ART-990 article-990-affidavit-of-response.... The receipt is honest that neither is rendered into the packet, calling each 'authority reference bound by digest; not a rendered component of this packet'. What does NOT bind is everything the packet actually renders. The Article 989 motion, the Article 991 order and the Article 992 order are composed, and no held bytes exist for any of them: I listed the Louisiana holdings of the Master Library and it carries Articles 984, 990, 993, 995, 998 and 999.1 and nothing else, so there is no copy of Articles 989, 991 or 992 in this container to compare the composed text against, and no legis.la.gov HTML capture either. The composition is authorized - I read the owner determination LA-STATUTORY-FORMS in data/rcap-grade-a/legal-decisions/OWNER_DETERMINATIONS_2026-09-02.json and it names this exact family, grants composition from authority of LA-CCRP-ART-988, 989, 991 and 992, lists remainOfficialAndMustBeHeld as empty, and says 'Do not wait for separate agency-issued fillable PDFs', so the builder's account of it is accurate. But the controlling legal record still carries the matter open: LA.memo.json track la-985-expungement-by-redaction, unresolvedQuestions item 1, impact release_blocker, affectedElement correct_form, reads 'Articles 987, 988, 989, 991, 992 and 994 - the Article 986 mandatory forms on which every Louisiana motion track depends - are retained by no Master Library Edition 1.1 asset... Confirm the canonical source form for each and adopt them in a successor edition before any Louisiana packet is released.' I confirmed that question's factual premise myself against the corpus. So the obligation is neither passed nor failed here: it is blocked on an open legal input, and the packet carries the question verbatim into participant-instructions.md line 149 rather than hiding it.

COMPONENT_SET.detail: The mechanical half checks out. The committed packet-set manifest declares six components: four required and generated (Article 989 primary_filing, Article 991 proposed_order, Article 992 proposed_order, and the instructions component at order 6), and two conditional and not generated (the Article 988 fee waiver and the Article 993 continuation), each recorded with the record's own condition text and a stated reason. All four required components are rendered and present, which I read off the delivered pages: 989 motion on packet pages 1-3, 991 order on page 4, 992 order on pages 5-6, instructions on pages 7-16. Neither conditional condition is met on either fixture, so requiredComponentsMissing measures 0. Two observations. First, MASTER_QUEUE.json lists four packetComponents for this family and names the fee waiver among them while omitting the instructions and continuation components the manifest declares; that is a queue-versus-manifest bookkeeping difference for Captain, not a packet defect, because the manifest is the authority. Second and controlling: LA.memo.json unresolvedQuestions item 4, impact release_blocker, affectedElement packet_components, asks 'Whether the Article 989 motion requires any distinct pleading or election to request redaction relief under Article 985 rather than full expungement, given that the redaction paragraph appears in the Article 992 order rather than in the motion'. That question is about whether this component set is the right one, it is open on the record, and I will not answer it in a verifier row. The build did not guess it either; it carried it verbatim into the guide and into approval-request.json for counsel.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: All 37 declared writes produce readable ink and print on the page they belong to; that half is sound. Six of them, however, are not facts. On the Article 989 motion the build writes: original_arrest_charges = 'Original arrest charge and statute for each count exactly as they appear on the state rap sheet', which is the field's own printed prompt written back into the field as its answer; disposition_type = 'Disposition wording from the canonical fixture court record'; underlying_entitlement = 'Article 977 - misdemeanor conviction, as the fixture court record states it'; other_individuals_named = 'One other individual is named in the record of this arrest, as the fixture record states'; others_entitled = 'Not known to the fixture participant'; record_locations = '...as far as the fixture participant knows'. Five of the six are written a second time onto the Article 992 PROPOSED ORDER OF EXPUNGEMENT, the document a judge signs, at packet page 5. The boundary fixture repeats the pattern with longer prompt-restatements. Every one of the six is a REQUIRED participantInput on the controlling record - originalArrestCharges, dispositionType, underlyingEntitlement, otherIndividualsNamed, othersEntitled, recordLocations - so these are facts the route needs and the platform did not hold. The correct treatment was available and the same builder used it seven times over: race, gender, the last four SSN digits, the arrest or booking number, the SID number, the agency item number and the driver's licence number are all classified REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, left visibly blank, and named in the guide's 'What you must supply before filing' table. These six were instead classified written, so not one of them appears in that table, and the guide's lead-in tells the participant to 'Check every prefilled fact against your own court record', framing them as facts to check rather than prompts to replace. Two consequences make this an output defect rather than a fixture nicety. The build-harness word 'fixture' is printed four times on the face of a motion and a proposed order. And the cell the Louisiana State Police list of common fatal errors singles out - the original arrest charge, which the guide itself warns at line 141 must not be the amended charge and must not omit counts - carries nothing but a restatement of its own question. No other family I read this shift does this: az_certificate_second_chance-set, fl-self-defense-set, hi_nonconviction_expungement-set and all three Illinois families supply real-shaped participant facts in every written cell.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: Coverage is otherwise very good: the guide carries all 20 registry items, all 6 selfHelpStopConditions, all 3 exclusions and all 4 unresolvedQuestions verbatim, numbered, with the count printed beside them, and all 7 blanks the field map classes REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING appear in the 'What you must supply before filing' table with what to write. The failure is a false statement about this packet inside a required-before-filing item. participant-instructions.md item 5 of 18, and again at the obtain_document entry, prints the record's howToObtain verbatim: 'The packet gives you the Article 988 form with your own fields filled in. Take or send it to the district attorney's office BEFORE the motion is filed.' This packet does not give the participant the Article 988 form. The guide itself says so 22 lines earlier, under 'What is not generated, and the condition the record states': the fee-waiver component 'is not generated'. The two statements are never reconciled, and the stakes are the Article 983(A) five-hundred-and-fifty-dollar cap, non-refundable even if the motion is denied, because item 5 also says 'Filing without it means paying the fee.' The builder solved exactly this problem for the OTHER not-generated component one line later - for the Article 993 supplemental sheet it adds 'ask the clerk of court for the Article 993 supplemental sheet rather than adding pages of your own' - and did not do the same for Article 988.

On the Article 991 order: the four ordering paragraphs, the no-contradictory-hearing finding, the return date, the date and place of the order and the judge's signature are all blank. On the Article 992 order: whether the motion is granted or denied, the findings, the decretal paragraphs, the date and place and the judge's signature are all blank. Both proposed orders carry a printed banner - 'COURT USE ONLY - UNEXECUTED PROPOSED ORDER. Nothing on this page has been decided, and no relief exists unless and until a judge completes and signs it and the clerk enters it' - so neither can be mistaken for an executed order. The Article 985 redaction paragraph, the one blank on the packet that most looks like the packet's to write, is left blank with the reason printed beneath it from Article 985(C), and the two mover-supplied facts the paragraph needs are printed above it so the court has them to hand.
